label: Boa
notes: A session builds the whole engine (nothing shared between sessions), applies its limits, registers the host call function, then evaluates 1 + 1 and reads 2 back in Rust. Limits: RuntimeLimits: loop_iteration_limit=1000000000, recursion_limit=512, stack_size_limit=10240; no memory limit API; Context::default has no I/O (no boa_runtime).
Memory: resident growth across 1,000 live sessions (stopped by target), measured first in a fresh process.

Tool call: the guest calls a registered Rust function on its own stack. Median of per-batch means, 1,000,000 calls in batches of 1,000 after 100,000 warm-ups; mean 2.5382 µs, slowest batch 424.5474 µs per call; 2.538 µs of CPU per call.
Session = Context::default() (full realm with intrinsics, default features float16/xsum/temporal) + runtime limits + global call.
Host fn is NativeFunction::from_fn_ptr registered with register_global_callable; reply built with ObjectInitializer and static js_string! keys.
boa_gc collects with stop-the-world mark and sweep: the median batch hides the pauses, so the mean and the CPU per call run well above the median, and the slowest batch includes a pause.
Compute: not measured in the Rust host.
